skill.name: use-link-identity
skill.description: Use Link CLI's identity commands when a service requests a Link Agent Attestation Token (AAT) or signed user claims such as email. Covers acquiring and managing attestations, obtaining identity credentials, and presenting selected claims to a verifier through an HTTP client or browser automation.
skill.summary: Manage Link attestations and present selected identity claims to an intended service using Link CLI.

content.user_title: Present Link Attestations and Identity Claims
content.value_statement: Services can require agent attestations or signed identity claims before accepting a request. This skill guides Link CLI workflows for obtaining proofs and presenting authorized claims.
actual_capabilities: Map service authentication challenges to attestation or identity presentation commands.
Guide attestation inventory checks, batch requests, token consumption, and batch exports.
Check credential availability, expiry, and available claim names before requesting issuance.
Generate presentations for a verified audience and nonce using selected authorized claims.
Guide exact proof handoff through endpoint-specific HTTP or browser headers.
Explain recovery for empty pools, unavailable claims, holder-key mismatches, and rejected challenges.
limitations: Requires Link Agent Wallet v0.27.0 or later; identity commands are in beta.
Identity commands require CLI access and are not available through Link MCP tools.
The receiving service must support Link proofs; acceptance and token reuse rules remain service-specific.
Callers manage exported token allocation, concurrency, and cleanup; separate users need separate home directories.

use_cases.title: Respond to an attestation challenge
use_cases.description: Inspect the local pool, obtain an AAT when needed, and pass its authorization value to the intended endpoint.

use_cases.title: Present an authorized email claim
use_cases.description: Use a verified audience and nonce to present only the email claim requested by the service and authorized by the user.

use_cases.title: Coordinate attestation allocation
use_cases.description: Export an attestation batch and plan token ownership, concurrency, and cleanup outside the internal CLI pool.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect identity readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Link CLI version and local identity inventory. Report availability and errors without exposing tokens, private keys, or claim values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect the environment before requesting proofs.

prompt_templates.title: Handle an attestation request
prompt_templates.prompt: Handle the PrivateToken challenge for [endpoint]. Check inventory and refill only if needed. Send the exact authorization value without logging it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: satisfy a service attestation challenge.

prompt_templates.title: Present selected claims
prompt_templates.prompt: Present only my authorized email claim to [endpoint]. Validate its audience and nonce, use safe process arguments, and report only the acceptance status.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: satisfy an identity challenge with minimal disclosure.

prompt_templates.title: Plan multi-agent token handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an exported AAT batch for [worker count] workers. Address permissions, allocation, concurrency, cleanup, identity isolation, and retries. Do not request tokens yet.

output_examples.input: Explain how to respond when the attestation pool is empty.
output: Request a new batch before attempting to pop a token.
Use the returned authorization value unchanged for the intended endpoint.
Keep token values out of transcripts and logs.

output_examples.input: Explain the checks before presenting my email claim.
output: Confirm that a usable credential includes the email claim.
Validate the intended service audience and current nonce.
Select only the authorized email claim and keep the credential and holder key local.
Report success only after the service accepts the request.

best_practices: Parse CLI JSON programmatically and keep proofs, private keys, and claim values out of transcripts and logs.
Validate the destination, audience, and nonce before presenting only claims authorized by the user.
Use separate home directories for different users and restrictive permissions for proof handoff files.
anti_patterns: Manually reconstructing tokens or presentations, or including them in logs.
Using global browser headers or forwarding identity proofs across origins.
Assuming an authentication change switches cached identity, or disclosing raw credentials instead of selected claims.

faq.question: What is the difference between an AAT and a presentation?
faq.answer: An AAT proves Link issuance without user claims. A presentation discloses selected claims and proves holder-key possession for an audience and nonce.

faq.question: Which Link CLI version is required?
faq.answer: Use Link Agent Wallet v0.27.0 or later. Identity commands are in beta and do not require a preview flag.

faq.question: Can I use these commands through Link MCP tools?
faq.answer: No. The documented identity commands are available through the CLI, not its MCP tools.

faq.question: Which operations require Link authentication?
faq.answer: Only request operations require Link authentication. List, pop, and present use local files.

faq.question: Does logging in as another user switch cached identity?
faq.answer: No. Cached identity belongs to the home directory. Use separate home directories for different users.

faq.question: Can I reuse attestations and presentations?
faq.answer: Keep an AAT for retries within an existing interaction, subject to service rules. Use fresh challenges after nonce consumption or expiry.
